title.narrative: SDG Target 5.3 – Campaign to End Child, Early and Forced Marriage (CEFM): Parliamentarians in target ODA-eligible countries have improved knowledge of CEFM and demonstrate political will to create an enabling legal and policy frameworks that, in addition to establishing 18 as the legal age of marriage for both boys and girls with no exceptions, also guarantees girls’ human rights, including those married and/ or in informal unions, in their equal access to education, sexual and reproductive health and rights, employment, justice and political participation.

Targeted parliamentarians take concrete actions to address CEFM as a human rights violation, crime against humanity and a development issue, such as: calling on the Executive and discussing/ introducing parliamentary initiatives, motions and resolutions strengthening legislation to promote and protect girls’ human rights.

target.value: PGA members in Kenya contributed to establishing a national strategy to end CEFM.

actual.value:
Because of disruptions due to the Covid pandemic and preparations for election campaigns, follow up to PGA's February 2021 in-person meeting in the Parliament of Kenya was delayed. PGA's Board Member in Kenya, Hon. Millie Odiambo, MP, will be sending an update on the status of the national strategy to end CEFM for inclusion in the June 30 narrative report.
In the meantime, I am pleased to report that, in 2022, PGA members undertook concrete actions to end CEFM in Ecuador and Malaysia.

target.value: Meetings of parliamentarians with civil society representatives and other key stakeholders to exchange information about CEFM in at least two ODA-eligible countries, including Kenya.

actual.value: Meetings of parliamentarians with civil society representatives and other key stakeholders to exchange information about CEFM were held in two ODA-eligible countries: Afghanistan and Kenya.

title.narrative: Parliamentarians in target ODA-eligible countries in Sub-Saharan Africa, Asia-Pacific, Latin America and the Caribbean, Middle East and North Africa (MENA) and Eastern Europe utilize the unique prerogatives of their offices to promote and protect human rights, democracy, peace and sustainable development, especially SDGs 5, 14 and 16.
Increased awareness, engagement and concrete actions taken by parliamentarians in support of SDGs 5, 14 and 16.
